summary: A halo you fold from one sheet of Japanese paper. Pull two opposite corners and all twenty-four pleats open at once. Thin solar cells on the outer pleats light the rim. Nobody has built one.
license_note: MIT is what this card's #vc-card block declares and what its page says in words — reproduce it, including selling it — and the same block declares replication "open". NOTICE at the repo root, served at https://mrdirno.github.io/vibe-cards/NOTICE.txt, is where this project withholds material it cannot grant; measured 2026-08-17, NOTICE names nothing belonging to this card — its only occurrence of "zaria" is inside a grep command quoted in another entry's prose — and this manifest adds no withholding of its own. The limit here is provenance, not scope: the package arrived from outside this repository carrying its own MIT at examples/zaria-card/docs/LICENSE and its own authorship note, and no commit in this repo records who made the front render. The grant over the artwork is that package's declaration repeated, not a verification of it.
origin: Not a fork and not a repository of its own: /zaria/ is a page-project inside mrdirno/vibe-cards (the GitHub API reports private=false, fork=false, default_branch=main, created 2026-08-10), published on that repo's Pages surface, so its MIT is both inherited from the repo's LICENSE and declared by the package. THE CARD ITSELF CAME FROM SOMEWHERE ELSE, and this is criterion 5's answer. examples/zaria-card is a folder generated by another system and handed over — the same route MOKU-003 took, whose README states it plainly: "It was generated somewhere else and handed over as a folder. It did not come from this repository and it is not a fork of anything in it." It entered the tree 2026-08-16 in commit 32184bf, which records what arrived: the QR and the chip payload both read https://compound-crafts.github.io/book-1/craft-006-zaria/, the card's metadata sat in a <div> rather than a <script> so tools/intake_card.py ran past it and died, and the QR occupied the 10.3 mm box at x 68.3 / y 36.7 that every front in this system reserves for the tap mark. That address has never resolved: measured 2026-08-17 it returns 404, and the GitHub account "compound-crafts" itself returns 404 from the users API against a 200 control on "mrdirno" in the same run, so there is no account behind the host. The front artwork arrived embedded in the drop rather than being made here — examples/zaria-card/package/index.html carries it as a base64 image/webp data URI, byte-identical (sha256 427dacba57833e78…, 483,776 bytes) to examples/zaria-card/assets/editorial.webp, which is on disk but untracked because .gitignore line 72 ignores *.webp. It is a synthetic render that shows a face, and the package declares that in three places: <meta name="ai-generated" content="true"> in package/index.html, the #vc-card provenance field, and docs/AUTHORSHIP.md ("AI: Image render synthetic muse"). No real person is depicted. The package also renamed itself before arriving: docs/EULOGY.md records "Renamed Aurelia -> Zaria for Card 6", which is why card 005 in this same book is separately named Aurelia. What this repository did is the intake: rewrote every occurrence of the address to https://mrdirno.github.io/vibe-cards/zaria/, regenerated the QR from the slug rather than editing it, moved it off the tap mark, moved the metadata into a <script>, and wrote the print artifacts with tools/intake_card.py. docs/FREEZE_MANIFEST.json's recorded sha256 c779f34e… no longer matches package/index.html (5b1243b9…); that mismatch is the record of the intake, not a corruption.
_note:
A page-project's manifest, published at the surface's own url. The network gate fetches <listed url>/wish-it-better.json, and https://mrdirno.github.io/vibe-cards/zaria/ is the address burned into this card's chip, so a person holding the card and nothing else can reach this file. Measured 2026-08-17: that path returned 404 before this file existed, which is the gap it closes and the reason it is hand-authored rather than derived — the builder only derives manifests for entries already in listed[], so a derived one would be produced BY the act of listing and criterion 4 would prove itself.

L0, and each of the three clauses was measured rather than assumed. (1) "This file present": WISH_IT_BETTER.md is tracked at the repo root and served at https://mrdirno.github.io/vibe-cards/WISH_IT_BETTER.md — 200, while /wish-it-better.md returned 404 in the same run, so the 200 is a real path and not a case-folding host. (2) "a wish channel that works": the wish_channel above is THIS page's own well, not the landing page's. data-wish-well appears exactly once in the page as SERVED (curl, 2026-08-17), which is what tools/verify_pages_artifact.mjs requires before it will accept an https channel at all, and the page returns 200 against .../zaria/control-404-for-the-wish-well-gate returning 404 on the same host in the same run. The endpoint the button posts to is byte-identical to src/site/_wish/config.json and answers 200 to an anonymous GET, against a 404 (PGRST205) control on a table name that does not exist. NOT MEASURED, and it matters: I did not submit a wish. An insert is a write and this pass was read-only, so "the queue accepts it" is carried from that config's own note (public anon key, RLS, insert-only, migration 079) and is not my observation. (3) "a LICENSE": the GitHub licence API returns spdx_id MIT, path LICENSE, for mrdirno/vibe-cards.

Not L1, on both of its clauses. "Every shipped change carries an eval meeting §2" cannot hold for an object that does not exist. The package's own docs/README.md lists what was never verified — no IV sweep performed, fold life beyond a thousand cycles estimated, caustics not lab-measured, the 38-minute assembly time borrowed from similar builds — and the page repeats all of it in a section of its own. §2's E1 asks for the observation that would have proven you wrong; nothing here has been built, so no such observation has been made about the halo, and the headline 3.6 W / 2.1 W is three assumptions multiplied whose own arithmetic lands at 2.75 W. "Wishes reach a terminal state" is not observable from here: the anon key cannot read the queue (the GET above returns [] under RLS), so no wish for this card can be shown to have reached claimed, shipped, declined or expired. The three entries in src/site/zaria/entries.json are defects caught during intake, not wishes worked to a terminal state. L2 is further off still: §5 says even the v1.0.1 amendment "earns nobody L2" because the origin project found it, and this card has contributed nothing to the spec, so amended is empty and honest.

Why the bare page url and not <url>/#wish. tools/build_site.py's derived manifest writes {SITE_ROOT}{slug}/#wish for a listed in-site entry. This page has no element with id="wish" — grep finds none — so that anchor resolves to nothing. The gate strips the fragment before fetching, so the anchor form would have passed the check while sending a card holder's agent to a fragment that is not there. The url above is the page itself, and it is the same string the chip carries.

What the fields cannot carry. THE ADDRESS CAN NEVER MOVE. src/site/network.json's cards block records this chip as LEDGER-DERIVED: `python3 tools/card_ledger.py --list` has a ZARIA-HALO-006 instance with a chip write to this url. That is a record that a write was ISSUED, not a tag read back; closing it needs the physical card on a reader and `python3 src/nfcio.py read`, and it is not closable from software. The chip carries the Pages path directly with no redirector in front of it, so if that host, repo name or path ever changes, this card goes dead and the only remedy is physical access to each printed copy. The same block records `./tools/qrdecode` returning this url from all four shipped front artifacts (measured 2026-08-16 by an earlier pass; I did not re-run it).

The package already contains a file named wish-it-better.json — examples/zaria-card/docs/wish-it-better.json — and it is NOT this one. It is the arriving system's own paperwork, kept verbatim the way MOKU-003's is, and it is not live configuration: it declares url https://compound-crafts.github.io/book-1/craft-006-zaria/, which 404s, and it carries no wish_channel, no license, no origin and no repo at all. A crawler that found it would read a manifest empty in the one field §4 says a machine reads.

One licence history worth keeping, because it is why this file states a licence instead of leaving it to the repo. examples/zaria-card/docs/LICENSE was 63 bytes — "MIT License" and a copyright line, no grant clause — until commit 47ba30c on 2026-08-17, while src/site/zaria/index.html told a stranger "This card is MIT. Do what you like with it, including sell it" and then explained a warranty clause that file did not contain. A copyright assertion with no grant is all-rights-reserved. The canonical MIT text is in that file now (1,088 bytes, three lines matching the grant and warranty clauses), copyright line unchanged as "Copyright (c) 2026 Compound Crafts CRAFT-006 ZARIA" — which is not the repo LICENSE's holder, "Aldrin Payopay / Persona 500 LLC", and that difference is left as the package set it.

If this entry is ever listed, the level here must equal the level badged in src/site/network.json or tools/build_site.py fails the build by design; that same arm keeps this authored file and does not overwrite it with a derivation.
